mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.5% for three consecutive months, it indicates a weak labor market that suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust economic expansion, which boosts corporate profits and investor confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for the interaction signal falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window, or positive returns occur in less than 45% of instances where both HOUST and INDPRO rise.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS rising above 0.5% annually), the increased cost of borrowing reduces corporate investment and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS > 0.5%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC is negative over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A positive quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) indicates sustained economic expansion, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of quarters with positive GDPC1 growth, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 2.5%, it signals rising inflation expectations that prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market (PAYEMS rising) combined with low interest rates (FEDFUNDS below 0.5%) indicates robust economic conditions and accommodative policy, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: strong labor and loose monetary policy
failure_condition: The Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window, or positive returns occur in less than 45% of instances where PAYEMS rises and FEDFUNDS < 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO falling below 90.0), it signals a contraction in manufacturing and supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO < 90.0, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC is negative over a 2-year rolling window.
